metadata.title: A quadratic family of integral two-torsion classes in a Huneke-Wiegand Koszul presentation
metadata.description:
For every integer p>=8, we prove that an explicit integral Koszul presentation associated with a previously constructed Huneke-Wiegand family has a direct summand (Z/2)^q, where q=floor(((p-2)^2+3)/12). The classes are indexed by the strictly increasing nonnegative triples i<j<k with i+j+k=p-2. Reflection-symmetric interval potentials give complete original-domain integer sources for twice each class; relative parity functionals with ten to twelve supporting K rows detect the classes independently. An elementary six-step counting argument gives the quadratic growth, and a vector-space extension argument gives the splitting. No explicit uniform global retraction or complete Smith form is claimed.

The proof includes an exhaustive classification of every source that can meet the functionals and a complete reconstruction of the D-kernel in every relevant high-variable sector, including the free diagonal potentials at the endpoint sector. It also proves exact order two for a previously tracked four-row connecting representative, constructs its original signed annihilator and its transfer to one triangle class, and gives a complete integral potential basis of rank binomial(p-1,2) in a neighboring sector with at most seven K rows per basis image.

Independent exact audits verify all 70 declared triangle sources, five representative-transfer identities, and 364 complete triangle-sector parity certificates at p=8,...,12. These certificates concern 27 functionals on 65 distinct sectors containing 23,695 distinct original S sources; repeated sector incidences are not counted as distinct matrices. Separate campaigns check 861 neighboring-sector chains, 18 full annihilators, and 2,123 complete-kernel potential chains. Every tested signed source is preserved in deterministic lossless archives. The uniform theorems follow from the complete symbolic proofs, not extrapolation from these finite checks.

Scope: this is a partial direct-summand decomposition of the full explicit integral presentation, not a classification of its entire cokernel, an upper bound, an identification with an isolated or relative-completion quotient, or a proof of the lower-strand recurrence. The family-to-presentation identification is an explicitly imported premise. Son Pham retains priority for the original public counterexample; this is a separate homological companion to the CAOS family record. The Jacobian conjecture is not addressed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
